# Contribution Guidelines
Thank you for the willingness to contribute!

## Guidelines
Before discussing about how you could contribute, please keep the following guidelines in mind to insure a safe environment, stability, and readability. Pull requests that do not follow the syntax or guidelines may be delayed or denied.

- Follow proper code syntax, see below.
- When creating pull requests it is advised that you create a new branch other than main and to commit on that branch only; this avoids issues during updating.
- We accept pull requests made with AI tools. However, you must insure that the implemented feature or change works correctly as expected, and that necessary tests are performed. Pull requests that do not follow this guideline will be rejected until such tests are performed. When you make a pull request that has code made with AI tools, you are responsible for performing the tests as you know the best of what prompts or how you did to construct the code.

### Code format
Use tab for indentation. Also, make sure operators are padded.

Good:
```
void test() {
	alert("hello", "testing");
}
```

Bad:
```
void test()
{
alert("hello","testing");
}
```

### Naming convention
- A class , method, function, namespace, and variable name must be snake lowercase, `my_class` is good, `myClass` and `MyClass` are not.
- The name of a constant variable, the one that never changes in runtime, must be snake uppercase, `MY_CONSTANT` is good, `MyConstant`, `my_constant`, and `myConstant` are not. This also applies to enum value names, but not the name of the enums itself. The name of the enum itself should be snake lowercase, i.e. just as the case of a namespace.

## Documentation Generator
### Overview
Documentation generator takes `.md` and `.nvgt` source files and turns them into HTML documentation and structured Markdown files with TOML front matter.

### Filenames and Folders
- Put `!` at the start of a filename if you want it to sort near the top. The `!` is removed from the output filename.
- Add `+` to the end of a filename stem to use the first line of the file as its display title. The `+` is removed from the output filename.
- Put `@` anywhere in a filename stem to make it a standalone root document. It gets its own HTML page and a link is added to the main document.
- Add `.MDRoot` to a folder to compile the whole folder into its own standalone document. The document is named after the folder.
- Add `.index.json` to a folder if you want to control the sort order and set custom titles for files manually.
- For normal filenames, leading symbols are removed and the remaining words are title-cased to create the display title.

### Scanning and Sorting
- If a folder has a `.index.json`, its items are processed in the order they appear in the file.
- Without an index file, everything is sorted alphabetically using the raw lowercase filename.
- Files are always processed before subdirectories at the same level.
- Files and folders starting with `.` are ignored, except for `.index.json` and `.MDRoot`.
- Only `.md` and `.nvgt` files are scanned.

### Code Files (`.nvgt`)
- Documentation is pulled from block comments that start with `/**` and end with `*/`.
- Normal `/**` comments have their lines trimmed, and non-empty lines are joined with blank lines to make readable paragraphs.
- `/**\` comments keep the original line breaks and spacing.
- The source filename is added at the top as the main `#` heading.
- Any line starting with `// example:` is automatically turned into a `## example:` heading.

### Heading Levels
- Headings in each file are adjusted based on how deeply the file is nested in the folder structure.
- Deeper headings are scaled down as needed, up to a maximum of `######`.
- Root documents created from `@` files or `.MDRoot` folders always start at `#`.
- If the first heading in a file matches the parent folder's display name, it is removed to avoid showing the same title twice.

### Output Files
- Markdown files are saved in `/MD/` with TOML front matter containing the document title,; this is used to put the documentation to the website generated by Hugo.
- HTML files are saved in `/HTML/` with basic styling and code-rendering options enabled.
- Code blocks in the HTML output automatically get language labels and copy buttons.
- The final output includes `docs.md` and `docs.html`, which contain all merged content except standalone root documents. `docs.md` is moved to the website's content directory.
